sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 10.0% a year, from $129 billion in FY2017 [F1] to $303 billion in FY2026 [F10][F203], while operating margin rose from 3.2% [F23] to 3.9% [F32].
The step change came in FY2021 and FY2022, when revenue grew 17.5% [D189] and 15.8% [D238], after 9.2% growth in FY2020 [D140].
Management attributed FY2021 net sales growth to comparable sales up 16% and new warehouses [P56], with higher gasoline prices also adding to sales [P55].
Growth then slowed to a 7.8% three-year revenue CAGR for FY2023 to FY2026 [D705], before FY2026 accelerated to 10.1% [D434].
Product net sales rose 10.1% [D534], contributing 9.9pp of growth [D535]; Warehouse ancillary and other businesses led at 3.7pp [D601], growing 19.9% [D600] with no cause in the cited passages.
Net sales rose 10% on comparable sales up 8%, driven by 5% higher average ticket and 3% higher shopping frequency [P14].
Warehouse ancillary and other businesses contributed most in FY2022 at 7.6pp [D589], where management said growth was strongest in gasoline, business centers and travel [P42].
Operating income grew 12.5% against 10.1% revenue growth in FY2026 [D435][D434], an incremental margin of 4.7% [D457] above the 3.9% operating margin [F32].
Diluted EPS grew 14.0% [D438] against 13.9% net income growth [D436], as diluted shares fell 0.1% [D452].
Operating margin of 3.9% [F32] is the window high [D691], against a window median of 3.4% [D692] and a low of 3.1% in FY2019 [D690].
The retail peer median operating margin is 5.0% [D710], placing the company at the 17th percentile [D709].
The FY2026 bridge was flat: cost of revenue had no effect and SG&A added 0.1pp [D459][D460], for a 0.1pp total rise [D447].
The largest move was FY2022, when cost of revenue cut 0.7pp [D263] as gross margin fell 65 basis points on core-category declines and a LIFO charge [P40].
SG&A added back 0.7pp [D264] as its ratio of sales fell 77 basis points, largely from leveraging increased sales [P38].
Operating cash flow of $15.8 billion was 1.71x net income of $9.23 billion [F82][F42][D421]; free cash flow was 1.02x net income, near the 0.99x window median [D422][D701].
Operating cash flow rose 18.6% in FY2026 [D439], which management linked to higher operating income and lower net inventory investment [P6].
Conversion bottomed in FY2022 at 0.60x [D699] as free cash flow fell 34.8% [D244], and the cited FY2022 operating cash passage gives no cause [P35].
Capital expenditure of $6.44 billion [F92] was 2.41x depreciation and amortization [D423] and 2.1% of revenue [D417], tied by management to new and remodeled warehouses [P46].
Net cash rose to $15.1 billion in FY2026 [D427], or 5.0% of revenue [D428], from $9.50 billion a year earlier [D378].
The 5.0% ranks at the 100th percentile of six retail peers, against a peer median of -4.4% [D715][D716][D428].
Buybacks and dividends took 35.2% of free cash flow [D430]: $848 million of repurchases [X110] and $2.46 billion of dividends [X120].
Diluted shares rose from 440.9 million in FY2017 [X91] to 444.4 million [X100], so per-share growth has tracked net income.
The pack lists no red-flag candidates, so these items come from screening the evidence.
Current debt rose to $2.25 billion from $75 million [X160][X159] while total debt grew 6.5% [D454]; the cited passages do not explain the change.
Tariff refunds flatter the latest year: $184 million was received in FY2026 [P15], and part was invested in member price cuts [P15], against a 3.9% operating margin [F32].
Free cash flow fell 34.8% in FY2022 [D244] to a 0.60x conversion low [D699], and the cited FY2022 operating cash passage is truncated and gives no cause [P35].
Operating margin holding at or above the 3.9% FY2026 level [F32][D691] would confirm the trend; a fall to the 3.4% window median [D692] would reverse it, shown in the FY2027 10-K.

Free cash flow to net income staying at or above the 0.99x window median [D701], against 1.02x in FY2026 [D422], would confirm conversion; a return toward the 0.60x low [D699] would reverse it, in the FY2027 10-K.

Whether the $2.25 billion of current debt [X160] is repaid or refinanced, and whether the $1.12 billion remaining buyback authority [P3], expiring January 2027 [P3], is renewed, will appear in the FY2027 10-K.
